chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If a servant performs Hajj ten times, there would still be upon him the Hajj of Islam as well, when he has the capacity to do so. And if a young boy performs Hajj ten times, then attains puberty, upon him would be the Obligation of Islam. And if an owned slave performs Hajj ten times, then is freed, upon him would be the Obligation of Islam, when he has the capacity for it.
ai.seo_question: Does performing Hajj ten times as a slave or child exempt one from the obligatory Hajj later?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that voluntary or pre-liability Hajj acts do not substitute for the obligatory Hajj al-Islam, even if performed ten times by slaves or pre-pubertal boys. It establishes a key principle in Shia jurisprudence that the 'Hajj of Islam' is a distinct, subsequent duty triggered only upon attaining full legal capacity (freedom for slaves, puberty for boys), ensuring the ritual's completeness is tied to the individual's mature status.
